bank_name: Original A1-B2 Conversational Placement Item Bank
content_policy: Every prompt was written specifically for this graduation-project MVP. No examination prompt, sample audio, or proprietary test content was copied or paraphrased.

items.main_prompt: Tell me what you usually do after you wake up and before you leave home.
items.main_clarification_prompt: Describe your morning routine from waking up until leaving home. Mention at least two things you do.
items.follow_up_prompt: Which part of your morning do you like most?
items.follow_up_clarification_prompt: Choose one part of your morning routine that you enjoy most and say what it is.

review.author: project_item_writer_ai_assisted
review.notes: Original, culturally neutral, no specialist vocabulary.

items.main_prompt: Tell me about one place near your home that you visit often. Say what it is and why you go there.
items.main_clarification_prompt: Name a place close to your home that you often visit, then give one reason you visit it.
items.follow_up_prompt: Who do you usually go there with?
items.follow_up_clarification_prompt: Say whether you normally visit that place alone or with another person, and name the person if you can.

items.main_prompt: Say what you normally eat or drink at the start of your day, and tell me which item you prefer.
items.main_clarification_prompt: Name food or a drink you usually have in the morning, then say which one you like best.
items.follow_up_prompt: When do you have something different?
items.follow_up_clarification_prompt: Say when you change that usual food or drink, for example on a weekend or a special day.

items.main_prompt: Tell me about two people you know well. Say who they are and one simple thing about each person.
items.main_clarification_prompt: Choose two people you know. For each person, say who the person is and give one simple detail about them.

review.author: project_item_writer_ai_assisted
review.notes: Does not require a conventional family structure.

items.main_prompt: You are in a shop. Ask for a notebook, choose a size or colour, and ask how much it costs.
items.main_clarification_prompt: Pretend you are speaking to a shop assistant. Ask for a notebook, say the size or colour you want, and ask the price.
items.follow_up_prompt: That notebook is sold out. Ask for a suitable alternative.
items.follow_up_clarification_prompt: The notebook you wanted is unavailable. Ask the shop assistant for a different suitable notebook.

items.main_prompt: At a bus station, ask for a ticket to a nearby city and find out when the bus leaves.
items.main_clarification_prompt: Pretend you are at a bus station. Say where you want to go, ask for a ticket, and ask the departure time.
items.follow_up_prompt: The next bus is full. Explain when you need to arrive and ask about another departure.
items.follow_up_clarification_prompt: That bus has no seats. Say when you need to reach the city and ask when another bus leaves.

review.author: project_item_writer_ai_assisted
review.notes: Does not depend on knowledge of a real timetable.

items.main_prompt: Make a phone appointment for a simple service. Say which day you want and ask what times are available.
items.main_clarification_prompt: Pretend you are calling to book an ordinary service. Ask for a day and ask which appointment times are free.
items.follow_up_prompt: Your preferred time is unavailable. Choose a different time and confirm it.
items.follow_up_clarification_prompt: The first time you chose is not free. Choose another time and clearly confirm the new appointment.

review.author: project_item_writer_ai_assisted
review.notes: Learner may choose any ordinary service.

items.main_prompt: You bought a small household item yesterday, but it does not work. Explain the problem to the shop assistant and ask for a replacement or refund.
items.main_clarification_prompt: Pretend you are returning a small broken item. Tell the shop assistant what is wrong and ask for a new item or your money back.

review.author: project_item_writer_ai_assisted
review.notes: Routine complaint without legal or technical knowledge.

items.main_prompt: Describe a time when a group task did not go according to plan. Explain what caused the problem and what the group did next.
items.main_clarification_prompt: Tell a story about a group activity that had a problem. Explain the cause and describe what the group did after the problem happened.
items.follow_up_prompt: If you led a similar group now, what would you organise differently?
items.follow_up_clarification_prompt: Imagine you lead that kind of group today. Say what you would change in the organisation and why.

review.author: project_item_writer_ai_assisted
review.notes: Accepts study, work, sport, or community examples.

items.main_prompt: Tell me about a skill you learned outside a formal class. Explain what was difficult at first and how you improved.
items.main_clarification_prompt: Choose a skill you learned without taking a normal class. Describe the first difficulty and explain how you became better.
items.follow_up_prompt: What advice would you give a beginner who wants to learn the same skill?
items.follow_up_clarification_prompt: Give practical advice to a person who is starting to learn that same skill.

review.author: project_item_writer_ai_assisted
review.notes: Broad domain gives learners equal access to personal experience.

items.main_prompt: Imagine you helped organise a small event and an important part failed at the last minute. Explain what happened and how you kept the event going.
items.main_clarification_prompt: Imagine a problem happened just before a small event. Describe the problem and explain what you did so the event could continue.
items.follow_up_prompt: What would you check earlier before organising another event?
items.follow_up_clarification_prompt: Say what you would prepare or inspect sooner next time to prevent the same problem.

review.author: project_item_writer_ai_assisted
review.notes: Hypothetical option avoids requiring a real event history.

items.main_prompt: A student works in the evening and keeps missing a morning course. Suggest two possible solutions, choose the better one, and explain why.
items.main_clarification_prompt: Give two ways to help a student who works at night and misses morning classes. Choose the better solution and give a reason.

review.author: project_item_writer_ai_assisted
review.notes: Familiar problem with multiple valid answers.

items.main_prompt: A company can offer students either fully remote internships or internships that require daily office attendance. Compare the effects on learning and access, then recommend a policy.
items.main_clarification_prompt: Compare internships done from home with internships done every day in an office. Discuss learning and who can access them, then recommend a company policy.
items.follow_up_prompt: Managers say remote interns receive less useful feedback. How does that affect your recommendation?
items.follow_up_clarification_prompt: Consider the claim that remote interns get weaker feedback. Explain whether this changes your policy and why.

items.main_prompt: A city has funding for either safer bicycle routes or more frequent buses. Compare the likely benefits and recommend where the money should go.
items.main_clarification_prompt: Compare spending city money on safer cycling routes with spending it on more buses. Discuss the benefits and choose one option.
items.follow_up_prompt: Some residents cannot cycle because of age or disability. Should the city change its choice?
items.follow_up_clarification_prompt: Think about people who cannot use bicycles. Explain whether that fact should change the city's decision.

review.author: project_item_writer_ai_assisted
review.notes: Tests qualification without requiring local policy facts.

items.main_prompt: A language programme can give every learner instant automated feedback or fewer sessions with a human tutor. Compare the two approaches and propose the best use of its budget.
items.main_clarification_prompt: Compare automatic feedback available to everyone with a smaller number of human-tutor sessions. Recommend how the programme should spend its money.
items.follow_up_prompt: Automated feedback can sometimes be confidently wrong. What safeguards would your proposal need?
items.follow_up_clarification_prompt: Automatic feedback may give incorrect advice. Describe checks or protections that would make your plan safer.

review.author: project_item_writer_ai_assisted
review.notes: Relevant to learners but answerable without AI expertise.

items.main_prompt: A training centre wants to let each learner choose completely flexible attendance times, but teachers argue that group progress will become unfair. Propose a policy that balances flexibility and fairness, and defend it.
items.main_clarification_prompt: Design an attendance rule that gives learners some choice but also keeps group progress fair. Explain the rule and defend your decision.

review.author: project_item_writer_ai_assisted
review.notes: Requires synthesis rather than a single obvious choice.
